guideTitle: 6 Best Knife and Scissor Sharpeners in 2026
metaTitle: 6 Best Knife and Scissor Sharpeners in 2026
metaDescription: Six electric knife and scissor sharpeners compared on angle options, abrasive stages, scissor slots and serrated support, with no prices.
introParagraphs: Most electric sharpeners are built for straight kitchen knives, and the scissor slot is a bonus that varies a lot between models. This guide looks at six sharpeners whose listings name scissors, and sorts out which ones give the scissors a dedicated port, which ones also mention serrated knives, and which ones simply offer an open slot for odd tools.

The key specs are the stage count, the abrasive, and the angle. The Maestri House 3-Stage Sharpener lists 360 grit and 600 grit diamond with a 1200 grit ceramic polish, the MrToNo 3-Stage Adjustable Sharpener offers six angles from 12 to 22 degrees, and the Work Sharp MK2 is a belt system instead of fixed wheels. We evaluated each pick based on product specs and buyer feedback.

Prices are left out on purpose. One honest caution first: many manufacturers limit slot sharpeners to straight edges and tell you to avoid the coarse stage on serrations, so read your model's instructions before sending scissors or a bread knife through any slot.

products.name: Maestri House 3-Stage Sharpener
products.description:
The Maestri House 3-Stage Sharpener spells out its grit ladder: 360 grit diamond to restore a dull edge, 600 grit diamond to refine it, and 1200 grit ceramic to polish. An adjustable 12 to 22 degree guide lets you match thinner Japanese-style knives, everyday Santoku and Western knives, and thicker cleavers. An 18W motor gives steady, low-vibration sharpening for home use.

A separate port on the left is set aside for scissors and specialty tools such as shears, axes, folding knives and flathead screwdrivers, while the polishing slot can be used for serrated edges according to the listing. Serrated support should still be treated with care, since many makers limit serrations to the fine stage only. A removable magnetic tray catches filings and an anti-slip base keeps the unit steady.

The layered options make it the most complete slot design in the group. Compared with the MrToNo 3-Stage Adjustable Sharpener, which lists a 3000 RPM motor and six named angles, the Maestri House publishes grit numbers, which makes expectations easier to set. It is more to learn than the fixed-angle Dawnstar S808 3-Stage, so expect to read the angle chart once.
products.bestFor: Home cooks who want published grit numbers, a scissor port and adjustable angles.
pros: Grit ladder of 360, 600 and 1200 is clearly stated
Adjustable 12 to 22 degree angle guide
Separate left port for scissors and tools
Magnetic tray catches metal filings
cons: Angle selection adds a learning step
Serrated use needs care with the coarse stage

products.name: MrToNo 3-Stage Adjustable Sharpener
products.description:
The MrToNo 3-Stage Adjustable Sharpener lists six named angles: 12, 14, 15, 18, 20 and 22 degrees. The listing suggests 12 to 14 degrees for Japanese fillet and fruit knives, 16 to 18 for Santoku and daily Western knives, and 20 to 22 for cleavers and heavier blades. A built-in 3000 RPM motor drives three stages, with stage one reshaping damaged edges, stage two refining, and stage three polishing.

The listing says it also handles kitchen scissors, household shears and axes, and mentions ceramic and serrated knives. The coarse and fine stages use diamond abrasives. The listing recommends using only the stages your knife needs, which is a sound habit. It does not publish grit numbers, unlike the Maestri House 3-Stage Sharpener.

Guided slots, a non-slip base and a removable magnetic collection tray round out the design. Compared with the fixed 20 degree Dawnstar S808 3-Stage, it gives you real angle control, which matters when you own a mix of knives. It is a step up in complexity from the Narcissus QN-M866 2-Stage, but it grows with a larger knife block.
products.bestFor: Cooks with a mix of Japanese and Western knives who want named angle presets.
pros: Six named angles from 12 to 22 degrees
3000 RPM motor drives all three stages
Diamond abrasives on coarse and fine stages
Removable magnetic tray eases cleanup
cons: No grit numbers published for the stages
More settings than a first-time user may want

products.name: KAZRBEP 5-in-1 Sharpener
products.description:
The KAZRBEP 5-in-1 Sharpener adds something none of the others offer: three motor speeds shown on an LCD display. The listing names the speeds only as low, medium and high, with no rpm figures. A 3-stage diamond system is listed for straight, serrated, cleaver and ceramic knives, scissors and axes.

A removable ceramic polishing bar handles specially shaped tools and adds a smooth finish. The listing instructs you to clip the knife in the slot, slide once and repeat three to five times per slot. A spring-loaded angle guide adjusts along the blade, with a fixed 20 degree clamp and an adjustable stop that extends to 32.5 degrees.

A bottom swarf plate collects metal chips, and removable parts ease cleanup. The 5-in-1 label is broad, so treat claims about axes and serrated blades as best-effort and check the model's instructions. Compared with the Maestri House 3-Stage Sharpener, it offers speed control rather than published grit numbers. It suits tinkerers more than first-time sharpeners.
products.bestFor: Users who want to dial the motor speed and add a polishing bar.
pros: Three speed settings with an LCD display
Removable ceramic bar for shaped tools
Spring-loaded guide holds angle along the blade
Swarf plate catches chips under the unit
cons: Broad 5-in-1 claims need a manual check
More controls than a one-button unit

products.name: Narcissus QN-M866 2-Stage
products.description:
The Narcissus QN-M866 2-Stage Sharpener keeps things basic with a crude stage that sharpens quickly and a fine stage that polishes to a burr-free edge. A 30-watt DC motor is stated to run for over an hour continuously, so you can work through the whole knife block without overheating. A 100 to 240V range makes it usable abroad.

The listing says to insert the knife at an angle, keep it against the outer wall and pull outside to inside, two to five times in each slot. A scissors slot on the side adds the extra function, and the listing suggests watching the product video before first use. A magnetic dust box under the unit collects filings.

It targets straight-blade kitchen knives such as chef, slicing and Santoku. Unlike the Narcissus S867 sibling, this listing does not mention ceramic or serrated knives. Compared with the Dawnstar S808 3-Stage, you lose a polish stage but gain a longer runtime story. It is the pick for people who want fewer decisions.
products.bestFor: People who want a simple two-slot design for straight kitchen knives.
pros: Simple crude and fine two-stage layout
30-watt DC motor runs over an hour
Side slot handles scissors
Magnetic dust box catches filings
cons: Listing does not mention serrated or ceramic use
Only two stages and no angle choice

products.name: Dawnstar S808 3-Stage
products.description:
The Dawnstar S808 3-Stage Sharpener offers repair, hone and polish stages with diamond abrasives. The coarse stage repairs dull or damaged edges, the fine stage hones, and the polish stage clears burrs. The listing says it handles straight, serrated, stainless and ceramic knives and quotes a 40 second repair time.

Fixed angle pads in each slot hold the blade at 20 degrees, which reduces the difficulty of use because there is nothing to adjust. An open-design port takes scissors, axes and other specialized tools. The tradeoff is rigidity: knives meant for a finer 15 degree edge would be reshaped to 20 degrees.

Compared with the Maestri House 3-Stage Sharpener and MrToNo 3-Stage Adjustable Sharpener, you give up angle control but get a quicker setup. Next to the Narcissus QN-M866 2-Stage it adds a polish stage. It is a good match for everyday Western knives that already sit near 20 degrees.
products.bestFor: Cooks with Western knives who want a fixed 20 degree, no-fuss design.
pros: Three stages for repair, hone and polish
Fixed 20 degree pads remove guesswork
Open port takes scissors and axes
Listing quotes a 40 second repair

products.name: Work Sharp MK2
products.description:
The Work Sharp MK2 is a different animal from the slot sharpeners. It uses flexible belts that conform to the edge, and the listing says they can sharpen outdoor tools, lawn mower blades, pocket and kitchen knives, even serrated knives and scissors. A two-speed motor gives control for light edge work and heavier grinding on axes and garden tools.

An edge guide supports the knife all the way to the tip. Work Sharp states a 3-year warranty and says it designs and calibrates the machines in Ashland, Oregon. The belt approach is more flexible, but it also asks for more technique than pulling a knife through a guided slot.

Compared with the Dawnstar S808 3-Stage or the Maestri House 3-Stage Sharpener, the MK2 handles a wider range of tools and belongs in a garage or workshop as much as a kitchen. It is not the quick pull-through of the Narcissus QN-M866 2-Stage. Pick it when pocket knives and garden tools matter as much as the kitchen block.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists who sharpen pocket knives, scissors and garden tools too.
pros: Flexible belts handle many edge tools
Two-speed motor suits light and heavy work
Edge guide supports the knife to the tip
Three-year warranty is stated
cons: Needs more technique than a slot unit
Overkill if you only sharpen kitchen knives

buyingCriteria.explanation: The angle sets how thin the edge is, and different knives want different angles. Adjustable units like the MrToNo 3-Stage Adjustable Sharpener (12 to 22 degrees) and Maestri House 3-Stage Sharpener suit mixed knife blocks. Fixed-angle models like the Dawnstar S808 3-Stage hold 20 degrees and remove guesswork. If you own Japanese knives meant for 15 degrees or less, an adjustable unit avoids reshaping them.

More stages let you separate repair from polish. A coarse stage reshapes damaged edges, a fine stage refines, and a polish stage clears burrs. The Maestri House 3-Stage Sharpener lists 360, 600 and 1200 grit, while the Narcissus QN-M866 2-Stage has only crude and fine. Use the coarse stage sparingly, because it removes the most metal.

A scissor slot is a bonus, not a given. The Maestri House has a dedicated left port, the Narcissus QN-M866 and Dawnstar S808 have a side or open port, and the Work Sharp MK2 uses belts. Many makers advise against putting scissors through the knife slots, so use only the port named for them. Check your model's instructions before trying.

Serrated blades have scalloped teeth that a through-slot wheel can chew. Some listings say serrated knives are supported, as with the MrToNo and Dawnstar S808, but makers often limit serrations to the fine stage and the smooth side. Never use a coarse stage on serrations. If bread knives matter most, consider a belt unit such as the Work Sharp MK2.

A steady motor matters more than a fast one. The MrToNo lists 3000 RPM, the Narcissus QN-M866 lists a 30-watt DC motor that runs over an hour, and the Maestri House lists 18W. The KAZRBEP adds low, medium and high speeds. Higher speed removes metal faster, so use low speeds for finishing.

Metal filings are fine dust, and a tray makes the difference between a quick wipe and a mess. The MrToNo, Maestri House and Narcissus QN-M866 each list a magnetic tray or dust box. A non-slip base keeps the unit planted so the knife stays level in the slot. Wipe the tray after every session.

howWeEvaluated.title: Angle and stage design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared adjustable angles against fixed 20 degree pads and counted stages. The MrToNo 3-Stage Adjustable Sharpener leads on named angle presets, and the Maestri House 3-Stage Sharpener leads on published grit numbers. Fixed-angle units were credited for simplicity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Scissor and tool support
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each listing treats scissors, axes and serrated knives. The Maestri House and Narcissus QN-M866 2-Stage have clear scissor ports, while the Work Sharp MK2 reaches the most tools. We marked broad claims as needing a manual check.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: Stated motor details were compared: 3000 RPM on the MrToNo, 18W on the Maestri House, 30-watt DC on the Narcissus, and speed settings on the KAZRBEP 5-in-1 Sharpener. Runtime claims, like the Narcissus one-hour figure, were noted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleanup and stability
howWeEvaluated.description: Magnetic trays, dust boxes, swarf plates and non-slip bases were reviewed. The KAZRBEP uses a bottom swarf plate and the others use magnetic trays. Stability counts because a rocking unit ruins an angle.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease and warranty
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed learning curve and any stated warranty. The Work Sharp MK2 lists 3 years, and the Dawnstar S808 3-Stage is the easiest to use. This rests on specs and buyer feedback, not lab measurement.

howToChoose.intro: Two ways to grind an edge.

cards.label: Slot wheels
cards.text: Abrasive wheels sit inside guided slots. You pull the blade through, and the guides hold the angle. The Maestri House, MrToNo, KAZRBEP, Narcissus QN-M866 and Dawnstar S808 work this way. It is fast and low-skill, but limited to straight edges in most cases.

cards.label: Belt system
cards.text: Flexible belts conform to the edge and can reach odd tools. The Work Sharp MK2 uses this approach with a two-speed motor. It handles more tool types but asks for steadier technique.

howToChoose.note: Slots for kitchens, belts for workshops.

howToChoose.intro: Not every pass needs the coarse stage.
howToChoose.note: Use the coarse stage only as often as the knife truly needs it.

howToChoose.intro: Treat scissors as a special case.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A dedicated scissors port or slot, not the knife slots. Read the manual first, since many makers forbid scissors in knife slots. Keep fingers clear of the blade path.

howToChoose.note: If a model does not name a scissors port, skip scissors.

faq.a: Several listings name scissors, but the safe method is to use only the port or slot they name for scissors. The Maestri House 3-Stage Sharpener has a left independent port, and the Narcissus QN-M866 has a side slot. Many makers advise against scissors in knife slots. Read your model's instructions first.

Some listings say yes, including the Dawnstar S808 and MrToNo. Makers' manuals often limit serrations to the fine stage on the smooth side, and the coarse stage can strip teeth. If bread knives matter most, consider a belt option like the Work Sharp MK2 or a manual rod.

Use the angle your knife was made for if you know it. Thin Japanese-style knives often sit around 12 to 15 degrees, and everyday Western knives near 16 to 20. The MrToNo and Maestri House let you choose, while the Dawnstar S808 fixes it at 20 degrees. When in doubt, go with 20.

Only when the knife struggles on tomato skin or paper. Over-sharpening removes metal for no gain. A light fine-stage pass is often enough, while the coarse stage is for real damage. The Narcissus QN-M866 listing suggests two to five pulls per slot.

faq.q: Are electric sharpeners safe for good knives?
faq.a: They remove more metal than honing rods, so use them sparingly on expensive knives. Adjustable models such as the Maestri House 3-Stage Sharpener let you match the factory angle. Skip the coarse stage unless the edge is damaged. For very valuable blades, a professional or whetstone is safer.

faq.q: How do I clean the filings?
faq.a: Unplug the unit and remove the magnetic tray or dust box. The MrToNo, Maestri House and Narcissus QN-M866 all list one, and the KAZRBEP has a bottom swarf plate. Wipe with a dry cloth. Clean the blade before sharpening, since dirt can damage the wheels.

A non-slip base keeps the unit steady, which matters if your hands are tired. Light pressure is enough. Do not press down or force the blade, because the wheels can stall. This is practical advice, not a medical claim.
